examples.en: We don't go to school tomorrow? Really?

examples.ko: 그 얘기 진짜예요? 저는 못 믿겠어요.
examples.en: Is that story true? I can't believe it.
Really? Our team won?
Is this price for real?

examples.ko: 진짜예요? 저도 그 가수 정말 좋아해요!
examples.en: Really? I like that singer a lot too!
Is this photo real, or is it fake?

explain: 놀랐을 때도 쓰고 사실인지 확인할 때도 써요. 같은 말인데 말하는 목소리에 따라 기쁜 놀람이 되기도 하고 의심이 되기도 해요. 친구 사이에서는 '진짜?'라고 하고, '정말요?'보다 조금 더 구어적이에요.

phrases.en: Really? Wow, I didn't know!
phrases.nuance_ko: 친구 사이에서 쓰는 반말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Casual speech between friends.

phrases.en: Really? I'm so happy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조금 더 단정해서 윗사람에게도 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Slightly more proper, so it can be used with seniors too.

phrases.en: Is it true? I can't believe it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사실인지 확인하는 느낌이 더 강해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Sounds more like checking whether something is true.

explain_en: You use it both when surprised and when checking whether something is true. The same words can sound like happy surprise or like doubt depending on your intonation. Among friends people say '진짜?', and it feels a bit more casual than '정말요?'.

examples.en: There's no exam tomorrow. Really?
Really? I didn't know that news.

examples.ko: 이거 다 먹어도 돼요. — 정말요? 고마워요.
examples.en: You can eat all of this. — Really? Thank you.
Really? Then let's go together!

examples.ko: 정말요? 그 식당이 벌써 문을 닫았어요?
examples.en: Really? That restaurant has already closed?
I'm going to Korea during vacation. Really? I'm jealous.

explain: 놀람이나 기쁨, 의심을 나타내는 반응이에요. '진짜예요?'와 비슷한데 '정말요?'가 조금 더 단정하게 들려서 윗사람에게도 쓸 수 있어요. 친구끼리는 '진짜?', '정말?'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: Really? I didn't know.
phrases.nuance_ko: '정말요?'보다 조금 더 편하고 구어적이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A bit more casual and conversational than the original phrase.

phrases.en: Really? Wow, how nice!
phrases.nuance_ko: 친구끼리 쓰는 반말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Casual speech between friends.

phrases.en: Is that true? I can't believe it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사실인지 확인하는 느낌이 더 강해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Sounds more like checking whether something is true.

explain_en: It shows surprise, delight or doubt as a reaction. It is close to '진짜예요?' but sounds a little neater, so it can be used with people above you too. Among friends, people say '진짜?' or '정말?'.

en: I see; oh, that's how it is

examples.en: Oh, I see. I understand now.
I see! I didn't know. Thanks for telling me.

examples.ko: 친구 설명을 듣고 “그렇구나” 하고 고개를 끄덕였어요.
examples.en: I listened to my friend's explanation, nodded and said “I see”.

examples.ko: 그렇구나. 그래서 어제 학교에 안 왔군요.
examples.en: I see. So that's why you didn't come to school yesterday.
The child said “oh, I see” with an amazed look.
I see, is that how people greet each other in Korea?

explain: 몰랐던 사실을 새로 알게 됐을 때 하는 반응으로, 반말이에요. 친구, 동생, 혼잣말에는 괜찮지만 윗사람에게는 '그렇군요'나 '그렇네요'를 써요. '-구나'는 새로 알게 된 것에 감탄하는 느낌이 있어요.

phrases.en: Oh, I see. Got it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 윗사람에게도 쓸 수 있는 존댓말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A polite form that can be used with seniors too.

phrases.en: You're right. I was wrong.
phrases.nuance_ko: 듣고 보니 맞다고 느낄 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you realize, after hearing it, that something is right.

phrases.en: Oh, is that so? I didn't know.
phrases.nuance_ko: 새 소식을 듣고 가볍게 반응할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used as a light reaction to new information.

explain_en: This is a casual reaction when you learn something new. It is fine with friends, younger people or to yourself, but with elders use '그렇군요' or '그렇네요'. The '-구나' ending carries a feel of realizing or marveling at something newly learned.

examples.ko: 시험에 떨어질 수도 있어요. 그럴 수 있지요.
examples.en: You can fail an exam. That can happen.

examples.ko: 그럴 수 있지요, 누구나 실수는 하니까요.
examples.en: That can happen, because everyone makes mistakes.

examples.ko: 괜찮아요, 그럴 수 있지. 다음엔 조심해요.
examples.en: It's okay, it happens. Just be careful next time.

examples.ko: 바빠서 연락을 못 했다고요? 그럴 수 있지요.
examples.en: You couldn't get in touch because you were busy? That can happen.

examples.ko: 처음이면 서툴러요. 그럴 수 있지, 천천히 해요.
examples.en: It's clumsy the first time. That's normal, so take it slowly.

examples.ko: 친구가 “그럴 수 있지” 하고 제 어깨를 두드렸어요.
examples.en: My friend patted my shoulder and said “it happens”.

explain: 상대의 실수나 사정을 이해하고 넘어갈 때, 위로하는 마음으로 해요. '그럴 수 있지'는 반말이고 '그럴 수 있지요'나 '그럴 수 있죠'는 정중한 말이에요. 화내지 않고 받아 주는 따뜻한 말투예요.

phrases.example: 그럴 수 있죠. 너무 걱정하지 마세요.
phrases.en: That can happen. Please don't worry too much.
phrases.nuance_ko: 정중하게 상대를 이해하고 위로할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to politely show understanding and comfort.

phrases.example: 그럴 수도 있어요. 다음에 잘하면 돼요.
phrases.en: That could happen. You can do well next time.
phrases.nuance_ko: '수도'를 써서 한 가지 가능성으로 부드럽게 받아들이는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Using the particle makes it sound like gently accepting one possibility.

phrases.en: It's okay. Anyone can do that.
phrases.nuance_ko: 실수한 사람의 마음을 편하게 해 주는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Puts the person who made a mistake at ease.

explain_en: You say it to understand and let go of someone's mistake or situation, with a comforting feeling. '그럴 수 있지' is casual, and '그럴 수 있지요' or '그럴 수 있죠' is the polite version. It has a warm, accepting tone without anger.

en: What should I do? / oh no

examples.en: I left my wallet at home. What should I do?
Oh no, I was late to the airport and missed my flight.
What if I'm late for the exam?

examples.ko: 어떡해! 새로 산 휴대폰이 물에 빠졌어요.
examples.en: Oh no! My new phone fell into the water.
I heard my friend is very sick. What should we do?

examples.ko: 발표 자료가 없어졌어요. 어떡해, 이제 시간이 없어요.
examples.en: My presentation file is gone. Oh no, there's no time left now.

explain: '어떻게 해'가 줄어든 말이라 걱정되거나 당황했을 때 문장 끝에서 감탄처럼 써요. '어떻게'는 '어떻게 가요?'처럼 동사 앞에 오는 부사이고, '어떡해'는 그 자체로 서술어여서 '어떡해 가요?'라고는 안 해요. 이 둘을 헷갈려서 잘못 쓰는 경우가 많아요.

phrases.en: I don't have my wallet. What should I do?
phrases.nuance_ko: '어떡해'를 풀어 쓴 말로, 문장 끝에서 '어떡해'와 같은 뜻으로 쓰고 조금 더 차분하게 들려요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is the spelled-out form of '어떡해'; it means the same at the end of a sentence but sounds a bit calmer.

phrases.en: I'm late for my appointment. What should I do?
phrases.nuance_ko: '어떡해'보다 혼잣말처럼 고민하는 느낌이 강해요.
phrases.nuance_en: It sounds more like thinking out loud and worrying than '어떡해'.

phrases.example: 우산이 없어요. 비가 많이 와서 큰일 났어요.
phrases.en: I don't have an umbrella. It's raining a lot, so I'm in trouble.
phrases.nuance_ko: '어떡해'처럼 걱정되는 상황에서 쓰지만, 일이 잘못됐다고 알리는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Like '어떡해' it shows worry, but it states that something has gone wrong.

explain_en: It is the contracted form of '어떻게 해' and works like an exclamation of worry or panic at the end of a sentence. '어떻게' is an adverb that comes before a verb, as in '어떻게 가요?', but '어떡해' is a predicate by itself, so you can't say '어떡해 가요?'. Learners often mix these two up.

en: What should I do?; Oh no

examples.en: I left my wallet at home. What should I do?

examples.ko: 어쩌죠? 비가 너무 많이 와서 못 갈 것 같아요.
examples.en: Oh no. It's raining so hard that I don't think I can go.
I'm late for our appointment. What should I do?

examples.ko: 어쩌죠? 제가 그 파일을 지워 버렸어요.
examples.en: Oh no. I deleted that file.
Oh dear. Were you badly hurt?
My friend keeps crying. What should I do?

explain: '어쩌지'는 반말이고, 존댓말은 '어쩌죠'나 '어쩌지요'예요. 내가 곤란할 때 혼잣말처럼 하기도 하고, 상대의 어려운 일에 안타까워하며 말할 때도 써요. '어떻게 해요?'와 비슷하지만 걱정하는 느낌이 더 강해요.

phrases.en: I left my wallet at home. What should I do?
phrases.nuance_ko: '어쩌지'의 존댓말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The polite form of the casual headword.

phrases.en: It's raining so hard. What should we do?
phrases.nuance_ko: '어떻게 해요'의 줄임말이고 걱정하는 느낌이 강해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A short form of 'what should I do', with a strong feeling of worry.

phrases.example: 큰일 났어요! 시험 시간을 잘못 알았어요.
phrases.en: Oh no! I got the exam time wrong.
phrases.nuance_ko: 문제가 크다고 놀랄 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when shocked that a problem is serious.

explain_en: '어쩌지' is casual speech; the polite forms are '어쩌죠' and '어쩌지요'. You can say it to yourself when you're in trouble, or to show sympathy for someone else's problem. It is close to '어떻게 해요?' but sounds more worried.

examples.ko: 선생님, 무슨 일이에요? 표정이 안 좋으세요.
examples.en: Teacher, what's the matter? You don't look well.

examples.ko: 옆방에서 웃음소리가 크게 들려요. 무슨 일이에요?
examples.en: I hear loud laughter from the next room. What's going on?
It's so noisy outside. What's going on?
Calling at this hour? What's the matter?

examples.ko: 친구가 울고 있어서 무슨 일이에요? 하고 물었어요.
examples.en: My friend was crying, so I asked, 'What's the matter?'

examples.ko: 갑자기 사람들이 모여 있네요. 무슨 일이에요?
examples.en: Suddenly a crowd has gathered. What's going on?

explain: 걱정되거나 놀랐을 때 이유를 물어요. 눈앞의 상황이나 갑자기 전화한 이유를 물을 때는 '무슨 일이에요?'가 자연스럽고, 상대에게 안 좋은 일이 있는지 걱정하며 물을 때는 '무슨 일 있어요?'가 더 자연스러워요. 친구에게는 '무슨 일이야?'라고 해요.

phrases.example: 얼굴이 안 좋아요. 무슨 일 있어요?
phrases.en: You don't look well. Is something wrong?
phrases.nuance_ko: 상대에게 안 좋은 일이 있는지 걱정하며 물을 때 더 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: More natural when you worry that something bad has happened to the person.

phrases.en: I asked my friend, 'What's going on?'
phrases.nuance_ko: 친구나 가까운 사람에게 쓰는 반말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The casual form for friends and close people.

phrases.en: Why are you acting like this all of a sudden? Are you sick?
phrases.nuance_ko: 상대의 행동이나 표정이 평소와 다를 때 이유를 물어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone's behavior or face looks different from usual.

explain_en: You ask this when you are worried or surprised and want to know the reason. '무슨 일이에요?' fits well for a situation in front of you or an unexpected call, while '무슨 일 있어요?' sounds more natural when you worry that something bad happened to the person. With friends say '무슨 일이야?'.

examples.en: I'm worried because of tomorrow's exam.
My child has a fever, so I'm worried.

examples.ko: 혼자 여행 가는 게 걱정이 돼요?
examples.en: Are you worried about traveling alone?
I was worried the roads might be jammed.
Lately I'm worried about my parents' health.

examples.ko: 비가 계속 와서 농사가 걱정이 되네요.
examples.en: It keeps raining, so I'm worried about the crops.

explain: '걱정하다'는 내가 걱정하는 행동이고, '걱정이 되다'는 걱정이 저절로 생기는 느낌이에요. '걱정되다'로 붙여 쓰기도 해요. 걱정되는 대상 뒤에는 '이/가'나 '때문에'를 써요.

phrases.en: I'm worried about the test results.
phrases.nuance_ko: '걱정이 되다'를 붙여 쓴 형태로, 말할 때 더 짧고 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A joined form of 'to be worried' that is shorter and more common in speech.

phrases.en: You look very sick. I'm worried.
phrases.nuance_ko: 친구나 가까운 사람에게 쓰는 반말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A casual form for friends and close people.

phrases.en: I have a lot of worries these days.
phrases.nuance_ko: 한 가지가 아니라 여러 걱정이 있을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you have many worries, not just one.

explain_en: '걱정하다' is the act of worrying, while '걱정이 되다' feels like worry arising on its own. It can also be written as one word, '걱정되다'. After the thing you worry about, use '이/가' or '때문에'.

examples.en: How do you feel today? — So-so.

examples.ko: 그 식당 음식은 그냥 그래요. 비싸기만 해요.
examples.en: The food at that restaurant is nothing special. It's just expensive.

examples.ko: 요즘 일은 어때요? 그냥 그래요. 조금 바빠요.
examples.en: How's work these days? Just so-so. I'm a bit busy.

examples.ko: 영화가 어땠어요? — 그냥 그래요. 별로 재미없었어요.
examples.en: How was the movie? — So-so. It wasn't very fun.

examples.ko: 새 직장은 그냥 그래요. 아직 적응 중이에요.
examples.en: The new job is so-so. I'm still adjusting.

examples.ko: 시험 결과는 그냥 그래요. 나쁘지도 좋지도 않아요.
examples.en: The exam result is so-so. Neither bad nor good.

explain: 좋지도 나쁘지도 않다는 뜻인데, 별로 말하고 싶지 않거나 기운이 없을 때도 자주 써요. '별로예요'는 더 부정적이고 '괜찮아요'는 더 긍정적이에요. 비슷한 '그저 그래요'도 있어요.

phrases.en: How are you these days? — Just so-so.
phrases.nuance_ko: '그냥 그래요'와 거의 같은 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Almost the same meaning as the main phrase.

phrases.en: That movie is not great. It's boring.
phrases.nuance_ko: '그냥 그래요'보다 더 부정적이고 마음에 안 든다는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: More negative; it means you don't really like it.

phrases.en: How does it taste? — It's average.
phrases.nuance_ko: 좋지도 나쁘지도 않은 보통 수준이라고 말해요. 기운이 없다는 느낌은 적어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Says it is at an average level, with less of a low-energy feeling.

explain_en: It means neither good nor bad, and people also use it when they don't feel like talking much or feel low. '별로예요' is more negative and '괜찮아요' is more positive. A similar phrase is '그저 그래요'.

examples.en: I went to the department store to buy earrings.
I lost one of my earrings.
I wear earrings every day.
A pair of earrings costs 20,000 won.
I put on a dress and wore earrings too.

explain: 귀걸이는 “귀고리”라고도 해요. 뜻은 같아요. 입는 것이 아니라 “해요”로 말해요: 귀걸이를 해요.

dict_examples.ko: 추운 겨울이라 두툼한 귀걸이를 하고 나갔다.
dict_examples.en: It was cold winter, so I went out wearing thick earmuffs.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.ko: 동생은 들어오면서 털실로 짠 귀걸이를 벗었다.
dict_examples.en: My younger sibling took off the earmuffs knitted from wool as they came in.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.ko: 밖이 어찌나 추운지 귀걸이를 해도 귀가 빨갛게 얼었다.
dict_examples.en: It was so cold outside that my ears froze red even with earmuffs.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.en: A round earring dangles by my sibling's ear.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.ko: 그는 반지와 귀걸이를 빼고 욕실로 들어갔다.
dict_examples.en: He took off his ring and earring and went into the bathroom.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.ko: 새로 산 귀걸이를 끼자 기분이 좋아졌다.
dict_examples.en: When I put on the newly bought earrings, I felt good.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.en: She likes to wear large earrings.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

explain_en: 귀걸이 is also called 귀고리, with the same meaning. The verb is 하다, not 입다: 귀걸이를 해요.

examples.ko: 팀장 임명 소식을 들은 팀원들이 박수를 쳤어요.
examples.en: The team members applauded when they heard the news of the team leader's appointment.

examples.ko: 임명 직후 새 대표는 조직 정비에 나섰습니다.
examples.en: Right after the appointment, the new CEO set about reorganizing.

examples.ko: 임명을 받은 날 부모님께 제일 먼저 전화를 드렸어요.
examples.en: On the day I received my appointment, I called my parents first.

examples.ko: 임명장 수여식은 내일 오전 열 시에 본관 강당에서 진행됩니다.
examples.en: The ceremony for presenting appointment letters will be held tomorrow at 10 a.m. in the main auditorium.

examples.ko: 공정하지 못한 임명이라는 비판이 직원들 사이에서 나왔어요.
examples.en: Criticism arose among staff that it was an unfair appointment.

explain: 임명(任命)은 윗사람이나 기관이 어떤 직책을 맡기는 일이에요. 받는 사람은 '임명되다, 임명을 받다'라고 해요. 투표로 뽑는 '선출'과 달라요.

dict_examples.ko: 각 부서의 부서장 임명 문제로 사장님께서 인사부장을 부르셨다며?
dict_examples.en: I heard the president called in the personnel manager about appointing department heads?

explain_en: 임명 (任命) is when a superior or organization assigns someone a post. The person who gets it says 임명되다 or 임명을 받다. It differs from 선출 (being chosen by vote).

examples.en: The baby laughed while touching his belly button.
Short T-shirts show your belly button.

examples.ko: 배꼽 근처가 갑자기 아파서 병원에 갔어요.
examples.en: The area near my belly button suddenly hurt, so I went to the hospital.
The baby's belly button sticks out. Is that okay?

examples.ko: 누워서 배꼽 위에 손을 올려 보세요.
examples.en: Lie down and put your hand over your belly button.

explain: 배꼽은 아기 때 탯줄이 있던 자리예요. 그 줄은 “탯줄”이라고 해요.

phrases.example: 배달비가 음식값보다 비싸다니, 배보다 배꼽이 더 크네요.
phrases.en: the tail wagging the dog; the extra costs more than the main thing
phrases.nuance_ko: 중심이 되는 것보다 덤이나 부수적인 것이 더 클 때 쓰는 속담이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: a proverb for when the extra part outgrows the main thing (lit. navel bigger than belly)
phrases.en_equiv: the tail wagging the dog; the extra costs more than the main thing

phrases.en: to split one's sides laughing
phrases.nuance_ko: 너무 웃겨서 배를 잡고 웃는 모습이에요. '배꼽 빠지게 웃다'라고도 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: laughing so hard you hold your belly; also said '배꼽 빠지게 웃다' (laugh until your navel falls out)

dict_examples.ko: 사과의 배꼽은 햇빛을 덜 받아서 녹색이다.
dict_examples.en: The navel of an apple is green because it gets less sunlight.

explain_en: The 배꼽 is where the umbilical cord was when you were a baby. The cord itself is called “탯줄”.
